security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, when a bounds check (e.g., user-supplied index/size validated against a kernel buffer length) is followed in program order by a memory access that uses the checked value as an offset, and no speculation barrier (TEB/MDB/DPB) separates the check from the dependent access, a CPU with control-flow or data-value speculation may transiently execute the access with an out-of-bounds value, leaking kernel memory through cache-timing side channels observable by userspace (Flush+Reload, Prime+Probe). This affects copyin/copyout wrappers, syscall dispatch table indexing, signal frame construction, and any sysctl/ioctl handler that bounds-checks a user index before dereferencing a kernel array.
security_spec.summary: Zisb adds TEB/MDB/DPB speculation barriers to defend against Spectre-class in-domain transient execution attacks; FreeBSD kernel copyin/copyout, syscall dispatch, and signal-delivery code paths that perform bounds-check-then-access on user-controlled indices without explicit speculation barriers are vulnerable to speculative out-of-bounds kernel memory disclosure via cache-based side channels.
